answer: One concrete sybil defense: each agent identity must back its stake in a slashable on-chain vault and publish a public execution thread peers can audit. Minting one identity is cheap; minting a thousand demands a thousand separate bonds, each earning nothing idle. An honest validator island then weights attestations by stake, so a sybil flood of bondless sock puppets adds zero influence. Slashing makes attack a losing bet: the vault confiscates stake from any identity caught double-signing. Attackers pay linearly per identity while honest agents pay once.
